title: Great Zimbabwe at its height
description: The stone-walled capital of a Shona kingdom trading gold to the Indian Ocean coast is the largest ancient structure south of the Sahara.

title: Kingdom of Mutapa founded
description: By tradition Nyatsimba Mutota leaves Great Zimbabwe and founds a new state in the north, near the Zambezi.

title: Khami becomes the capital of Butua
description: As Great Zimbabwe declines, the Torwa rulers build a new stone capital in the south-west.

title: Silveira killed at the Mutapa court
description: The Jesuit Gonçalo da Silveira baptises the king and is then put to death, giving Portugal a pretext for invasion.

title: Mutapa becomes a Portuguese vassal
description: Mavura, installed with Portuguese help, signs a treaty that gives them control of the kingdom's mines and trade.

title: Changamire Dombo defeats the Portuguese
description: The Rozvi ruler beats a Portuguese force and in the following years drives the Portuguese off the plateau.

title: Ndebele kingdom founded
description: Mzilikazi leads his people north across the Limpopo and sets up a kingdom that dominates the south-west.

title: Livingstone sees the Victoria Falls
description: The missionary David Livingstone reaches the falls on the Zambezi and names them after the British queen.

title: Rudd Concession
description: King Lobengula grants mining rights to agents of Cecil Rhodes, who uses the document to obtain a royal charter for his company.

title: Pioneer Column reaches Fort Salisbury
description: Settlers and police of the British South Africa Company occupy Mashonaland and raise the flag at the site of the future capital.

title: First Matabele War
description: Company forces with Maxim guns defeat the Ndebele army and occupy Lobengula's capital.

title: Risings against company rule
description: The Ndebele and then the Shona rise against the British South Africa Company in the war later called the First Chimurenga.

title: Self-government for Southern Rhodesia
description: After the settlers vote against joining South Africa, company rule ends and Southern Rhodesia becomes a self-governing British colony.

title: Land Apportionment Act
description: The law reserves about half the land, including most of the best, for the small white minority.

title: Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland
description: Britain joins Southern Rhodesia to what are now Zambia and Malawi in a federation that lasts ten years.

title: Kariba Dam opened
description: The dam on the Zambezi forms what is then the largest man-made lake in the world, displacing about 57,000 Tonga people.

title: Unilateral Declaration of Independence
description: Ian Smith's white minority government declares independence from Britain rather than accept majority rule.

title: Battle of Sinoia
description: Seven ZANLA guerrillas are killed by Rhodesian forces in the clash later counted as the start of the liberation war.

title: Lancaster House Agreement
description: The Rhodesian government and the guerrilla movements agree a ceasefire, a constitution and elections under British supervision.

title: Independence
description: Zimbabwe becomes independent under majority rule with Robert Mugabe as prime minister.

title: Gukurahundi
description: The army's Fifth Brigade kills thousands of civilians, mostly Ndebele, in a campaign against supposed dissidents.

title: Unity Accord
description: Mugabe's ZANU and Joshua Nkomo's ZAPU merge, ending the violence in Matabeleland and leaving the country in effect a one-party state.

title: Farm occupations begin
description: After voters reject a draft constitution, war veterans and others occupy white-owned farms, the start of a land redistribution that is followed by economic collapse.

title: Hyperinflation peaks
description: Prices almost double every day before the Zimbabwe dollar is abandoned for foreign currencies.

title: Mugabe removed
description: A week after the army takes control of the capital, Robert Mugabe resigns after thirty-seven years in power and Emmerson Mnangagwa succeeds him.
